description: HDR metadata (HDR10, HDR10+, Dolby Vision) decomposed. HDR delivery requires the decoder/display to know the content's mastering luminance range and how to map it to the display's capabilities. Static metadata (HDR10) provides one mapping for the whole stream; dynamic metadata (HDR10+, Dolby Vision) provides per-scene guidance. Each format encodes the metadata as SEI messages in the bitstream — extensible without changing the codec.

sub_mechanisms.name: mastering_display_metadata
sub_mechanisms.definition: MDCV / SMPTE ST 2086: specifies the mastering display's primaries, white point, and luminance range. Sent once per stream as SEI.
sub_mechanisms.why: Tells the player what display the content was authored on. Lets the renderer adapt the tone mapping for displays that differ from the mastering display. Standard for all HDR formats.

sub_mechanisms.name: content_light_level_info
sub_mechanisms.definition: CLLI / SMPTE ST 2086 supplement: MaxCLL (peak luminance found in the stream) and MaxFALL (average luminance across all frames). Sent once per stream.
sub_mechanisms.why: Gives the display a quick complexity estimate: a stream with MaxCLL=4000 nits needs aggressive tone mapping on a 1000-nit display; MaxCLL=300 fits any HDR display unchanged. Avoids needing to peek at the actual frame data.

sub_mechanisms.name: HDR10_static_curve
sub_mechanisms.definition: PQ + BT.2020 + 10-bit + MDCV + CLLI. Static metadata — one mapping per stream. The simplest HDR format.
sub_mechanisms.why: Backward-compatible with the broadest HDR ecosystem. No per-scene metadata = simpler authoring + lower bitrate overhead. But less adaptive — bright scenes and dark scenes share one tone curve, suboptimal for both.

sub_mechanisms.name: HDR10plus_dynamic_metadata
sub_mechanisms.definition: SMPTE ST 2094-40: per-scene dynamic metadata describing how to map source luminance to display luminance. Encoded as SEI with per-frame curve parameters.
sub_mechanisms.why: Different shots have different luminance distributions. Static metadata averages; dynamic adapts. A dark indoor shot can use the display's full range without needing to crush highlights for the bright outdoor shot it'll cut to. Royalty-free (Samsung-led).

sub_mechanisms.name: Dolby_Vision_dynamic_metadata
sub_mechanisms.definition: Proprietary dynamic metadata format from Dolby. 12-bit color, more detailed tone mapping parameters than HDR10+. Carried as proprietary SEI or as a dual-layer enhancement.
sub_mechanisms.why: Tighter end-to-end control; higher bit depth (12 vs 10); proprietary licensing covers display side too. Trades adoption breadth (HDR10+ is open) for higher per-display fidelity. Used heavily in iOS/Apple TV/some smart TVs.

sub_mechanisms.name: scene_change_anchors
sub_mechanisms.definition: HDR10+ and Dolby Vision metadata is anchored to shot boundaries: each new shot gets its own curve. Mid-shot adjustments are smooth interpolations.
sub_mechanisms.why: Discrete shot changes are perceptually unambiguous boundaries. Aligning metadata with shot changes avoids visible tone-curve jumps mid-scene. Mid-shot smooth interpolation handles slow lighting changes.

sub_mechanisms.name: tone_mapping_curve_parameters
sub_mechanisms.definition: Per-scene parameters: target peak luminance, midpoint anchor, knee point (where tone curve compresses highlights), shoulder roll-off shape.
sub_mechanisms.why: Compact representation of a tone-mapping curve as 4-8 numbers. Lets the player reconstruct the curve at runtime. Encoded as a small bitstream chunk (~100 bytes per shot).

sub_mechanisms.name: scene_max_average_luminance
sub_mechanisms.definition: Per-scene MaxCLL and MaxFALL, refining the stream-level values to per-shot accuracy.
sub_mechanisms.why: Stream-level CLLI is conservative (designed for worst case). Per-shot values let the display dispute that worst case for dimmer shots, avoiding over-compression of highlights in scenes that don't have any.

sub_mechanisms.name: fall_back_to_static
sub_mechanisms.definition: Dynamic-metadata HDR formats also include the static (HDR10) metadata. Players that don't understand HDR10+/DV fall back to HDR10 mode.
sub_mechanisms.why: Backward compatibility: a non-HDR10+ player still gets a valid HDR experience via the static metadata. Dynamic features degrade gracefully. Required for ecosystem deployment because not all displays support dynamic.

sub_mechanisms.name: sei_message_carriage
sub_mechanisms.definition: Both HDR10+ and Dolby Vision carry their metadata in user-defined SEI messages (NAL unit type 6, payloadType 4 + custom identifier). The codec itself doesn't process the metadata.
sub_mechanisms.why: Codec-agnostic delivery: same SEI works in H.264/H.265/H.266/AV1. The decoder passes the SEI through to the rendering pipeline; the rendering layer processes it. Lets HDR metadata be added/changed without codec versioning.

derivation_rules.name: dynamic_metadata_outperforms_static_on_varied_content
if: content has wide shot-to-shot luminance variation
then: dynamic metadata produces better tone mapping than static
derivation_rules.why: Static metadata's one-curve-fits-all averages across shots. Per-shot dynamic curves can optimise each. The advantage scales with content variety; cinematic content benefits more than news/documentary.

derivation_rules.name: sei_carriage_enables_codec_agnostic_metadata
if: HDR metadata is carried in SEI
derivation_rules.why: SEI is the codec's standard extension mechanism. Carriage of HDR metadata via SEI lets streaming pipelines mix codecs (AV1 + Dolby Vision metadata, for instance) without redefining the metadata format.

derivation_rules.name: fallback_static_preserves_compatibility
if: dynamic-metadata HDR format includes static metadata
then: older HDR10-only players still display the stream correctly
derivation_rules.why: Backward compatibility is the deployment constraint. Including both metadata layers costs ~100 bytes per shot but covers the entire installed base of HDR10 displays. Trade-off heavily favours inclusion.

derivation_rules.name: scene_boundary_anchoring_prevents_visible_curves
if: metadata changes are anchored to shot boundaries
then: tone curve transitions are not perceptible
derivation_rules.why: Mid-scene curve changes would shift brightness/colors visibly. Shot boundaries are already perceptual discontinuities; metadata changes there are masked by the cut. Mid-shot smooth interpolation handles slow lighting changes without abrupt transitions.

derivation_rules.name: proprietary_format_trades_breadth_for_fidelity
if: a format is proprietary with controlled licensing
then: it can offer higher fidelity at the cost of ecosystem breadth
derivation_rules.why: Dolby Vision controls encoder + display + processing; can optimise the whole pipeline. HDR10+ is open and works on more displays but can't dictate display-side processing. Same fundamental trade as Dolby Atmos vs DTS:X.
